response.sql: WITH pairs AS (SELECT s.transref, t.tradekind, AVG(s.anlycount) AS avg_anly FROM sentimentandfundamentals s JOIN transactionrecord tr ON tr.transreg = s.transref JOIN trader t ON t.tradereg = tr.trdref GROUP BY s.transref, t.tradekind HAVING AVG(s.anlycount) IS NOT NULL), overall AS (SELECT AVG(avg_anly) AS mean_avg FROM pairs), kept AS (SELECT p.tradekind, p.avg_anly, p.avg_anly - o.mean_avg AS excess FROM pairs p CROSS JOIN overall o WHERE p.avg_anly > o.mean_avg), per_type AS (SELECT tradekind, AVG(avg_anly) AS avg_analyst_count, AVG(excess) AS avg_excess_over_mean FROM kept GROUP BY tradekind) SELECT tradekind, avg_analyst_count, avg_excess_over_mean, avg_analyst_count / AVG(avg_analyst_count) OVER () AS relative_ratio FROM per_type ORDER BY tradekind

assumptions.assumption: A pair is (transref, trader type). Each transaction has one trader, so each transaction forms one pair. Pairs whose anlycount values are all NULL have no average and are excluded from the overall mean and from the kept set.
The overall mean is the unweighted mean of the pair averages. It is not weighted by the number of snapshots per pair.

The ratio divides each trader type's average analyst count (over its kept pairs) by the plain mean of that figure across the trader types that appear in the output. Types with no kept pairs are not returned.
